summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, multiple kidney and pancreas transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and chronic heart failure was admitted for hypotension, lethargy, and diarrhea. She presented with discolored dialysis fluid, raising concern for peritonitis, but cultures and cell counts were negative. She was volume resuscitated with 1.5 liters of normal saline, which improved her blood pressure. The red-tinged dialysis fluid was found to have minimal blood, with stable hemoglobin and a CT scan showing no acute abnormalities. Viral gastroenteritis was suspected as the cause of diarrhea, with negative C. diff and blood cultures. Tacrolimus was reduced due to a high level, and oral vitamin B12 was switched to monthly intramuscular injections due to poor absorption. Warfarin was held for a supratherapeutic INR and restarted at discharge. She improved clinically, remained euvolemic, and was discharged to extended care with medication adjustments and outpatient follow-up plans.
